name: Saddle Horse
notes: The ordinary riding horse. Good for thirty miles a day, and it will tell you before it quits.

name: Cow Pony
notes: Short, quick, and worth its weight at a cutting. Turns on a coin and knows the work better than the man on it.

name: Mustang
notes: Caught wild and never entirely agreed to this. Fast, hard-footed, and liable to take exception.

name: Draft Horse
notes: Built to pull, not to run. Two of them are a wagon team.

name: Mule
notes: Surer-footed than a horse in bad country, and a better judge of a bad idea. It will not be argued into a mine shaft.

name: Burro
notes: The prospector's whole freight line. Carries more than it has any right to.

name: Ox
notes: Slow past bearing and stronger than anything else in the yoke. Emigrant wagons ran on them.

name: Pack Mule Train
notes: Six animals on a lead rope. Treat the string as one thing until something spooks it, then don't.

name: Buckboard
notes: A plank seat over an axle. One team, two people, and whatever fits behind them.

name: Wagon
notes: The farm and freight wagon. Bows and canvas make it a home; a broken axle makes it a landmark.

name: Freight Wagon
notes: Three tons of goods behind six oxen or eight mules. It does not turn around on a narrow road.

name: Chuckwagon
notes: The drive's kitchen and its parliament. Losing it costs more morale than blood.

name: Stagecoach
notes: Nine inside and on top, a strongbox under the driver's boot, and a fresh team every twelve miles. The reason road agents exist.

name: Buggy
notes: One horse, two people, and a folding top. Town transport that will not survive open country.

name: Handcar
notes: A pump car on the line. Only goes where the rails go, and only as long as someone keeps pumping.

name: Rowboat
notes: Oars and a bailing can. Anything larger than a man in the water is a serious problem.

name: Canoe
notes: Quiet, quick, and unforgiving. Poles through shallows a boat would ground in.

name: Keelboat
speed: 15 ft upstream · as the river down
notes: Poled, cordelled, and cursed upriver. Carries a season's freight and a crew that fights.

name: Ferry
notes: A flat deck on a rope or a cable. The crossing costs coin, and the ferryman knows what's been in the water lately.

name: Riverboat
notes: A sternwheeler with a boiler that would rather explode than disappoint. Decks, cabins, and a saloon full of strangers.

name: Locomotive & Cars
notes: Engine, tender, express car, coaches. Unstoppable in a straight line and helpless anywhere else.

name: Rail Boxcar
notes: A rolling room with a door that latches from outside. Stock, freight, or whoever is riding without a ticket.
